module: Floating name labels above players' vehicles (multiseat and split screen). Uses the Skia billboard system (WorldBillboardRenderer object registered "playerNameTags" in MissionGroup): each label is a static texture from a `.sktemplate.json` template, tinted with the player's color, turned toward the camera, following the car, growing with distance (up to a cap) and disappearing beyond 40 m. Driven by core_multiseat (rebuild, updatePositions, reset…). Global: render_playerTags.
notes: Templates: 'default' = art/sktemplates/multiplayer-nametag.sktemplate.json; 'multiseat' = art/sktemplates/multiseat-player-tag.sktemplate.json. An unknown template name falls back to 'default'. Only 'multiseat' adds a persona icon (SVG from ui/ui-vue/src/assets/fonts/bngIcons/svg/<icon>.svg, filled in white); the icon name must be alphanumeric (^%w+$).
Colors: {r,g,b} between 0 and 1, blended toward an anthracite gray (54,69,79) at 30% (top) and 60% (bottom of the gradient); tintAccent replaces the color of 'accent' role nodes with this gradient.

Each rebuild entry: {player, label, color={r,g,b}, icon?, key?, perspectivePlayer?, hideInViews?}. The state is keyed by `key` (default player), which allows several labels per player (one per view in split screen). perspectivePlayer = the player who is looking: their own label only appears for 3 s (TAG_SHOW_TIME) after a change of vehicle occupancy or of vehicle; the others' labels stack vertically (0.33 m, 0.24 m with icon) above the vehicle.

Local tuning values: scale 0.36, max distance 40 m, minimum scale reached at 3 m and maximum at 26.7 m, switch to the seat position under 7 m, position smoothing 10. When the game is paused (simTimeAuthority.getPause) the labels are forced visible; in photo mode (photoModeOpen) they are hidden.

The base position is computed above the vehicle's oriented bounding box (OOBB), at the driver node level; otherwise 1.25 m above the vehicle's position. With multiple seats, gameplay_seatOccupants.getSeatExitData gives the position of each seat.
If the C++ object playerNameTags disappears (reload), liveRenderer detects it and clears the local state; reset() is also bound to onExtensionUnloaded.

destroy.desc: Destroys all current labels (billboards) and clears the local state, leaving the renderer in place.

reset.desc: Destroys the labels, forgets the renderer reference and clears hidden players and color overrides. To be called before a Lua/GE reload that destroys the C++ object; also onExtensionUnloaded.

onExtensionUnloaded.desc: Alias of reset called when the extension is unloaded.

isLive.desc: Indicates whether the billboard renderer exists in the scene.

returns.desc: true if the playerNameTags object exists.

hasTags.desc: Indicates whether at least one label exists.

rebuild.desc: Rebuilds all labels: stores the request (for reload and color overrides), destroys the old ones, creates the renderer if needed then one billboard per entry while keeping the previous smoothing state.

tags.desc: List of entries {player, label, color, icon?, key?, perspectivePlayer?, hideInViews?}.

returns.desc: false if tags is not a table or if the renderer could not be created.

reload.desc: Clears the template and SVG icon path caches then rebuilds the last requested labels (useful for tuning a .sktemplate.json).

returns.desc: false if there is nothing to rebuild.

setPlayerHidden.desc: Hides or shows a player's label.

setPlayerColorOverride.desc: Forces a color on a player and rebuilds the labels.

clearPlayerColorOverrides.desc: Removes the forced colors and rebuilds.

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Vehicle switch hook: updates the vehicle tracked by the player's labels; the label of the player who is looking is shown for 3 s.

updatePositions.desc: To be called every frame: computes position, (smoothed) scale and visibility of each label (grouping by vehicle, stacking, distance to the player's camera) and calls WorldBillboardRenderer:update.
